info.name: Jawab API — Mobile App Simulation + Admin
info.description:
Full API coverage for the Jawab backend (backend-admin), split into two top-level folders:

- MOBILE APP (ma/*): every endpoint the not-yet-built mobile app would call — register/login flow, profile, follow, topics, communities, posts, comments, polls, feed, search, subscriptions, notifications, media.
- ADMIN (admin/*): the full admin-panel-equivalent flow — login, dashboard, moderation, subscriptions/payments, bulk ops, exports.

Requests are ordered to run top-to-bottom via Postman's Collection Runner: login/create requests have test scripts that auto-capture tokens and IDs into collection variables, so later requests (e.g. Get Post By ID) work without manual copy-pasting.

One manual step: after 'Register', check the backend-admin server console for a line like 'Verification code for john@example.com: 123456' (SMTP is usually unconfigured locally) and paste it into 'Verify Email' before running 'Login'.

Base URL defaults to http://localhost:3001/api — change the base_url collection variable if needed.

Phone-based registration/login/verify/forgot-password is now supported (auth_type=phone, phone_number field) alongside email — see the '(Phone)' requests in MOBILE APP > 1. Auth. Since there's no real SMS provider wired up, phone flows write to a mock 'SMS box' (see MOBILE APP > 15. SMS Box (dev)) and every response also returns the OTP/reset code directly as dev_verification_code / dev_reset_code — unconditionally, not just in a dev environment.

item.name: MOBILE APP (ma/*)
0. NEW USER JOURNEY (ordered walkthrough)
item.description: Screen-by-screen simulation of the mobile app's first-run experience, in the exact order a new user would tap through: Sign Up -> Verify -> Complete Profile -> Choose Topics -> Join Communities -> Home Feed -> Polls -> Ask a Question -> Profile -> Logout. Unlike the domain-grouped folders below, this one is ordered by user journey, not by API resource, and generates a fresh random identity each run (via a pre-request script on step 01) so it's safely re-runnable now that username/email/phone_number are unique-constrained. A separate 'Forgot Password' mini-flow (F1-F2) covers the alternate path from the Login screen.

item.name: E. Forgot Password (alternate path from Login)

request.description: Screen: 'Reset my Password' (+965 phone field) -> SEND CODE. Uses the same phone as the signup flow above — run 01 first, or set journey_phone_number manually to an existing account's phone.

Screens: 'Enter Verification Code' + 'Set a New Password' combined into one API call — the mobile app holds the code across two screens, then submits code+new password together here. Leads to 'New Password Created' -> 'Get into the App' (re-login).
